title: Development charges hearing adjourned to April
subtitle: Brief special meeting: one complaint withdrawn, in-camera session on negotiations and land disposition, by-laws confirmed.
overview: Kitchener's special Council meeting on March 9, 2026 was short. Council agreed to adjourn the hearing on a development charges complaint about 15 Dellroy Avenue until no later than April 20, 2026 {{vote:m1}}. The hearing is about whether the City has jurisdiction to consider the complaint under Section 20 of the Development Charges Act.

A second, similar complaint, about 1438 Highland Road W, was withdrawn from the agenda. The minutes say it had been appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal and so was no longer within the City's jurisdiction.

Council then agreed to meet in closed session after the open meeting to consider a position or procedure for negotiations and a potential land disposition {{vote:m2}}. The minutes report no outcome from that session. The meeting also confirmed its actions through a by-law, and no delegations or mayoral business items came forward. For residents, the main effect is that both development charges matters will not be decided at this meeting.

decisions.detail: Council granted the request to adjourn the Section 20 development charges complaint hearing until no later than April 20, 2026.
Council authorized an in-camera meeting right after the special meeting to consider a position or procedure for negotiations and a potential land disposition.

debate: There was little debate. The transcript shows the Finance and Corporate Services chair noting that one development charges item had been removed from the agenda.
The other development charges item was deferred to April 20 on a motion put forward and seconded by councillors, with no discussion recorded before the vote.
No delegations were registered, and no councillor raised concerns about the closed-session motion or the by-laws.
